tasks.text: Rewrite a job description to strip out jargon and inflated requirements
tasks.reasoning: You supply the JD; the model transforms it. Language transformation on material you provide is the center of its competence.

tasks.text: Turn a page of your messy interview notes into a structured debrief
tasks.reasoning: Your notes in, structure out. The model never needs to know anything you didn't hand it.

tasks.text: Explain what happened to attrition in your Denver office last quarter
tasks.reasoning: The model never saw your attrition data. It will answer anyway — fluently, and invented.

tasks.text: Draft three versions of a candidate rejection email at different levels of warmth
tasks.reasoning: Tone variation on a well-understood format. It has seen thousands of these.

tasks.text: Summarize the themes across 200 engagement survey free-text comments you paste in
tasks.reasoning: Good at surfacing patterns, but it flattens minority views and will present a confident summary of the comments it weighted most. Read the raw comments too.

tasks.text: Tell you which section of your employee handbook covers bereavement leave
tasks.reasoning: It has never seen your handbook. It has seen thousands of others, so what it produces will read exactly like yours — and won't be.

tasks.text: Generate interview questions for a competency you describe in detail
tasks.reasoning: You describe the competency; it generates against your description. Supply the material, ask for transformation.

tasks.text: Recommend the comp band for a new role
tasks.reasoning: Your comp philosophy, your bands, your market data — none of it was in training. Any number it gives is a fabrication wearing a confident face.

tasks.text: Rewrite a policy paragraph so a non-native English speaker can follow it
tasks.reasoning: Plain-language rewriting of supplied text. Squarely in competence.

tasks.text: Explain, in general terms, what a statutory leave entitlement typically covers
tasks.reasoning: Reasonable in the abstract, unreliable on your jurisdiction, your plan, or current specifics. Verify anything you'd act on.

tasks.text: Decide whether an employee's conduct warrants termination
tasks.reasoning: This one isn't about capability. It's a decision about a person's livelihood and it stays with a human, however good the output looks.

tasks.text: Draft a performance improvement plan from notes you supply
tasks.reasoning: Structure and language, yes; the judgment about whether a PIP is warranted, never.

tasks.text: Tell you what your CEO said at last month's all-hands
tasks.reasoning: It wasn't in the room and the transcript wasn't in its training. It will produce plausible executive remarks that nobody gave.

tasks.text: Produce a plain-language FAQ from a benefits summary you paste in
tasks.reasoning: Pasted source, transformed format. The model has everything it needs because you gave it everything it needs.

tasks.text: Identify which of your open roles is hardest to fill
tasks.reasoning: Your requisition data never reached it. Same failure as the attrition question: a confident answer built on nothing.

pattern: AI does well when you supply the material and ask for transformation. It does badly when the task needs organizational knowledge it was never given. And it must not make decisions about people.
postscript: If you missed several, look at which kind you missed. Over-assigning to "does this well" means you're likely to ship something fabricated. Over-assigning to "does this badly" means you're leaving real leverage on the table. Both are calibration errors. Neither is a character flaw. Both are fixable, and the next seven modules are how.
